model: Sum of parts: unlevered owner-FCF DCF of the continuing IDC operating businesses plus co-investment portfolio and Capital Release Unit at haircut NAV, less debt, hybrids and leases (engine route)

equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR Investments segment: $2.5b co-investment portfolio, mostly units in Lendlease-managed unlisted funds. 10% haircut for unlisted-NAV lag and recycling friction. Its income is excluded from the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Capital Release Unit at 80% of invested capital (base)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR CRU segment: $3.6b invested capital after FY26 impairments, of which $0.9b contracted. The $720m erosion covers a further ~17% mark-down on the uncontracted $2.7b plus wind-down holding costs ($196m of segment operating costs in FY26), international construction tail liabilities and time to realise. CRU EBITDA is excluded from the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Perpetual subordinated hybrid securities at face
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note 17.d: $908m carrying amount net of $13m costs. Classified as equity, ranks ahead of ordinary securities; distributions are not deducted in operating EPS.
FY26 AR note 22; lease treatment A.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY27 IDC guidance, $8.4b construction backlog and nominal growth thereafter; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every historical CAGR is negative or undefined and none is a forecast base. Revenue fell from $10.4b (FY23) to $5.4b (FY26) because international construction, communities and other businesses were sold or moved to the CRU; equity fell on $2.5b of cumulative statutory losses FY22-FY26 (the FY26 equity figure of $4,825m also includes $908m of hybrids, so ordinary equity fell faster: -16% a year over 3 years); EPS and owner FCF are negative at one or both ends. SBC-adjusted FCF is $29-46m a year below reported FCF, immaterial against flows of -$0.1b to -$1.4b.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY26 -1,399; FY25 -874. SBC is only disclosed in the employee-benefits note, not on the cash flow statement, and was not backfilled for earlier years.

scenario_narratives.base: The reset lands, late and at a cost. FY27 IDC earnings meet the 37-41 cent guidance on pre-sold apartment settlements (One Circular Quay, Victoria Harbour) and conversion of the $8.4b construction backlog at about a 4% EBITDA margin; Investments earnings fall as guided because co-investments are recycled and FY26's transaction profits do not repeat. After the FY27-28 completion peak the continuing businesses earn roughly $450m of EBITDA after corporate cost (before co-investment income) and grow with nominal activity, retaining about $80m a year in the development book. The CRU is wound down for 80% of its $3.6b carrying value after holding costs and further marks, the co-investment stake realises 90% of NAV, and the proceeds take gearing toward the 15% target without new equity. The whole thing is worth roughly book value to ordinary holders once the hybrids are counted as the debt-like claim they are.
scenario_narratives.bull: New management executes what the last one promised. CRU exits clear at 92% of book inside two years, co-investments hold NAV, and gearing reaches target early enough for the buyback the Board has already flagged. The $13.2b Australian development pipeline and the Crown Estate joint venture seed new funds, funds under management turn from $43.9b back to growth, and the develop-to-core model lifts the margin on the continuing businesses toward 9.5% before SBC with growth of 4-5% through the middle years. Construction holds its recovered margin on defence, health and data-centre work. Value is roughly 1.4x ordinary book, which requires several independent things to go right.
scenario_narratives.bear: The pattern of FY19-FY26 continues. Uncontracted CRU assets (US and UK development, retained construction tail liabilities) realise only about 55% of book after another round of impairments and two more years of $150-200m holding costs; unlisted fund NAVs fall with higher Australian rates and the co-investment stake is sold at 80%. FY27 guidance is missed as cost inflation squeezes fixed-price construction and development feasibilities, funds under management keep shrinking, and the continuing businesses settle at a 6.7% owner margin with 2% growth. Gearing stays near 30%, the ratings are at risk, and an equity raise near the current price becomes likely; that dilution is not in this number, so the bear value should be read as generous to existing holders.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Lendlease is valued as a levered pool of assets, not as a cash-flow compounder. About 60% of base-case asset value sits in two bridge items marked off the balance sheet (the CRU and the co-investment portfolio) and 40% in a DCF of the continuing developer, contractor and funds platform. The price is about 0.47x ordinary NTA of $4.81 (not the published $6.16, which includes the hybrids) and implies roughly a 25% haircut across all assets; the base case implies about 8%. The gap between price and value is therefore almost entirely a disagreement about CRU realisation and whether an equity raise is needed, and the valuation is only as good as those carrying values. The hurdle entry price discounts the operating flows at 15% but takes the bridge assets at the same haircut values, so it is less conservative than it looks for a name where most of the value is in the bridge.
key_risks_to_valuation: CRU carrying values: each 10pp of recovery on the $3.6b is about $0.52 per security; FY26 alone took $773m of statutory loss on a $4.6b opening balance
Dilutive equity raise if gearing (30.3% reported, ~37.7% excluding the hybrid benefit) is not brought down by asset sales; not modelled in the share count
Hybrid step-ups from October 2028 (A$450m, margin +5.00%) and September 2030 (S$400m, +2.00%) make the $921m effectively debt with a refinancing date
IDC earnings quality: FY27-28 lean on a small number of large apartment completions; FY26 Investments EBITDA included $136m of transaction and other income
Unlisted fund NAVs and development feasibility are both exposed to further RBA tightening; 57% of debt is floating
The internal debt allocation behind IDC EPS is undisclosed, so the mapping from guidance to unlevered EBITDA (interest ~$165m pre-tax allocated to IDC in FY27) is an estimate
Scenario asset recoveries are routed through the capex line in years 1-3 of bear and bull; the dashboard sliders for capex in those years move asset recovery, not capital spending

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.26-5.50, so the quote is at the bottom of the range
data_sources.financials: LLC.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt (segment note 1.a, performance and outlook, financial position, notes 17, 22, 35.g); LLC.AX_Metrics.csv

inputs.share_count_basis: 691m stapled securities on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note 17), including 9m treasury securities held to satisfy employee awards. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows and awards are met from on-market treasury purchases. A dilutive equity raise is a bear-case risk that is NOT modelled in the count (see notes).
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report note 35.g: $29m expense for equity-settled security based payment awards (FY25: $46m). No equity-award tax line exists (awards are settled from treasury securities bought on market: $44m FY26, $26m FY25). Group figure; ~0.5% of revenue applied to the IDC flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build: ~4.6% Australian 10-year government bond + 5.5% ERP x ~1.25 beta (levered developer/contractor) = ~11.5% cost of equity; ~6% pre-tax debt (5.2% average cost of debt FY26, 57% floating, BBB-/Baa3) = ~4.2% after tax; 65/35 equity/debt target mix gives ~9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows and the asset haircuts, not the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt): lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; the $217m lease liability (FY26 AR note 22) is deducted once in the equity bridge; right-of-use renewal is covered by the maintenance part of the capex line (~0.9% of revenue against D&A of 0.8%).
inputs.nci_treatment: External non-controlling interests are $29m of book equity; deducted once in the bridge at book. Flows are not reduced for NCI.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Lendlease straddles four rows of the dcf-methods routing table: a funds manager, an inventory-heavy developer, a contractor, and a wind-down asset pool (the Capital Release Unit, CRU). Consolidated reported FCF (-$1,370m FY26, negative in 9 of the last 12 years) is dominated by development production spend and divestment timing and is not a usable base, so the parts are valued separately and summed: (1) the continuing IDC operating businesses (Construction, Development, Investments management platform and transaction income, net of allocated corporate cost) on an UNLEVERED component owner-FCF DCF at WACC; (2) the $2.5b co-investment portfolio at a haircut to NAV in the bridge, with its ~$75-87m of co-investment income stripped from the flows (matching-asset rule); (3) the CRU ($3.6b invested capital) at a haircut to book in the bridge, with its EBITDA excluded from the flows; less (4) statutory net debt, hybrids at face, lease liabilities and NCI. IDC operating EPS guidance is post-interest on an internal debt allocation that is not disclosed, which is why the flows are built pre-interest and the whole of group debt is deducted once. base_revenue is IDC segment revenue FY26 (Investments 282 + Development 655 + Construction 3,869); it is engine scaffolding, about 80% construction pass-through, so the EBITDA path matters and the revenue path mostly does not. last_fcf is the consolidated owner-FCF figure for audit only and is NOT the projection base. REPORTED NTA IS OVERSTATED FOR ORDINARY HOLDERS: the published 616 cents includes $908m of perpetual hybrids that are classified as equity but rank ahead; NTA to ordinary securityholders is (4,825 - 908 - 595) / 691 = ~$4.81 and book value ~$5.67. Operating EPS is also struck before hybrid distributions (~$41m a year: S$400m at 3.90% and A$450m at 5.20%, stepping up from October 2028 and September 2030). SCENARIO ASSET VALUES: the equity bridge is common to all scenarios and carries BASE recoveries (CRU 80% of book, co-investments 90% of NAV). Bear and bull recoveries are expressed as cash through the capex line in years 1-3 (bear: $1,150m shortfall; bull: $682m excess), so capex_pct_path in those years is not a view on capital expenditure. EQUITY-RAISE RISK: reported gearing is 30.3% including a 7.4pp hybrid benefit, against a 5-15% target, interest cover is 2.5x and the ratings sit at the lowest investment-grade notch. If CRU sales slip, a raise at a price near the current one is plausible; that dilution is not in the share count and is reflected only through the 40% bear weight. LEVERAGE: asset value in the base case is ~$8.3b against ~$4.9b of prior claims, so each 10% change in total asset value moves the per-security value by roughly $1.20.

bear.capex_note: Years 1-3 carry a $1,150m asset-realisation SHORTFALL against the base bridge (~$400m, $400m, $350m) on top of the normal 2.3% capex: CRU at 55% of book rather than 80% = -$900m; co-investments at 80% of NAV rather than 90% = -$250m. Not a capex view. Owner FCF is therefore negative in years 1-3 of this scenario by construction.

base.ebitda_margin_note: IDC EBITDA after allocated corporate cost, EXCLUDING co-investment income, BEFORE SBC. Year 1 = ~$481m on ~$5.5b revenue: FY27 guidance midpoint of 39 cents (OPAT ~$270m) plus ~$115m of after-tax allocated interest implies IDC NOPAT of ~$380m and EBITDA after corporate of ~$545m; less ~$75m co-investment income (moved to the bridge), less ~$17m for corporate cost stranded when the CRU closes, plus ~$28m SBC shown on its own line. FY26 equivalent was ~$360m (421 - 87 + SBC). Fades 0.3pp after FY28 as the One Circular Quay / Victoria Harbour completion peak passes.
base.capex_note: 0.9% maintenance and lease renewal (group capex $13m + lease principal $64m in FY26) plus 1.4% (~$80m a year) growth capital retained in the development book, about 3% of the $2.8b invested. Development profit is only cash if capital recycles; this line is the charge for growing it.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Below the 30% statutory rate because Trust income is flow-through and equity-accounted profits arrive after tax. Segment operating tax was 20% of segment pre-tax profit in FY26 and 24% in FY25 including low-taxed co-investment income, which is excluded here.
base.terminal_note: Cap of 14x binds (Gordon at 9.0% / 2.5% is ~15.8x). Cyclical, no-moat developer and contractor.

bull.capex_note: Years 1-2 carry ~$341m a year of asset-realisation EXCESS over the base bridge ($682m: CRU at 92% of book rather than 80% = +$432m; co-investments at 100% of NAV rather than 90% = +$250m) as a cash inflow, net of the normal 2.3% capex. Not a capex view.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 40%, well above the 15% house default: statutory losses in four of the last five years, the 15% gearing target already missed once, ratings at the lowest investment-grade notch, interest cover of 2.5x, and an equity value that is a thin residual over $4.9b of prior claims. Base 45%: guidance is supported by pre-sales and backlog, $0.9b of CRU sales are contracted, and FY26 marks were taken ahead of a new CEO. Bull 15%, below the 35% default: it needs clean CRU exits, a turn in funds under management and sustained margins together, from a management team that has not yet shown any of the three.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
